t: Founded by Manco Inca in 1537, it kept the Inca monarchy, court and Sun cult alive in the mountains of Vilcabamba until 1572.
Its rulers combined guerrilla war with diplomacy, and Titu Cusi’s account of 1570 gave an Inca view of the Spanish conquest.
Viceroy Toledo’s army took Vilcabamba in 1572, and the execution of Túpac Amaru in Cusco ended independent Inca rule.
dyk: Hiram Bingham III reached the ruins of Vilcabamba at Espíritu Pampa in 1911, but believed that Machu Picchu, which he had also explored that year, was the last Inca refuge.
ev: Manco Inca rebels and besieges Spanish-held Cusco for some ten months
Manco repulses the Spaniards at Ollantaytambo, then withdraws to Vitcos and Vilcabamba
Gonzalo Pizarro invades Vilcabamba; Manco escapes but Cura Ocllo is captured
Manco Inca is murdered at Vitcos by Spanish fugitives he had sheltered
Sayri Túpac renounces his claims in Lima and settles at Yucay
Titu Cusi Yupanqui accepts the Treaty of Acobamba
Titu Cusi dictates his account of the conquest for Philip II of Spain
Spanish forces take Vilcabamba; Túpac Amaru is captured and executed in Cusco
